html:
The third ecumenical council of the Christian church, called by Emperor Theodosius II and held at Ephesus in 431.

The fight was over how to speak of Christ and his mother. Nestorius, archbishop of Constantinople, objected to calling Mary Theotokos, "God-bearer", because it seemed to mix Christ's divine and human natures. Cyril of Alexandria insisted on the title. Cyril opened the council before the bishops from Antioch, who backed Nestorius, had arrived, and it deposed Nestorius. The Antiochenes held a rival council. Politics and imperial pressure decided the outcome, and a compromise was patched up in 433.

The council made Theotokos standard in Greek and Latin Christianity and boosted devotion to Mary. Nestorius died in exile. The Persian Church of the East, already organised at the Synod of Seleucia-Ctesiphon, never accepted Ephesus and was wrongly called "Nestorian" by its rivals. The quarrel went on and led to the Council of Chalcedon in 451.
sum: The third ecumenical council of the Christian church, called by Emperor Theodosius II and held at Ephesus in 431.
